items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: The interviewee discusses Tampa Red and Lester Melrose in the context of the interviewer's statement about Tampa Red recording for Melrose. The interviewee does not claim a personal relationship with Melrose, only responding to the interviewer's narrative about Melrose's business dealings with Tampa

ctx.x: Oh yeah, man. He's still making records. But I can't think of his first name now. Jazz Piuma? I'll play some one. He lived right at 35th and State. Tampa Red used to live along in there. That's the man I'm trying to call, Tampa Ray. But, but, but, but, uh, never to call him Tampa Ray. Yeah. But his real name is Roosevelt. Oh, is that right? I never do. Yeah. Tampa Ray, yes then. I thought his name was Hudson Whittaker. He put a harmonic in his mouth and put a guitar back there. I thought his name was Hudson…

No, then Mama Yancey used to call him Mrs. She'd meet and say, I saw Mrs. Tampa over at the market yesterday at the store. Mrs. Tampa. He used to record for Lester Melrose, and Lester always owed him royalties and so on. They'd get together. Yeah.

Do you remember the tunes you cut with Tampa Red? Well, I can't call the name of them. Some blues I know. Well, we'll look them up someday. Yeah, let's look them up. You see my name on there, all right?
